locator: ## DNS debugging toolkit — "# Query the systemd-resolved cache specifically\nresolvectl query --cache-only=yes example.com"
problem: resolvectl query has no --cache-only option, so this command errors out. The cache-related flag is --cache=BOOL, and --cache=yes is the default (it enables cache use, it does not restrict the lookup to the cache). To answer only from the local cache without issuing network requests, the correct flag is --network=no.
correction: Replace with `resolvectl query --network=no example.com` (answers only from cache/synthesis, never the network). If the intent is to demonstrate cache toggling, note that --cache=BOOL is the real flag and that --network=no is what forces a cache-only answer.

Could not refute the auditor; independently confirmed via two authoritative sources distinct from the auditor's Debian manpage: the man7.org resolvectl(1) man page and the Ubuntu noble resolvectl(1) man page. Both confirm every part of the finding.

The flagged command (docs/operations/dns.md line 359): `resolvectl query --cache-only=yes example.com`

1) --cache-only does NOT exist. Neither man page lists it; both explicitly state it is not a documented option. The full option list is -4/-6, -i/--interface, -p/--protocol, -t/--type, -c/--class, --service-address, --service-txt, --cname, --validate, --synthesize, --cache, --zone, --trust-anchor, --network, --search, --raw, --legend, --stale-data, --relax-single-label, --no-ask-password, --json, -j, --no-pager, -h/--help, --version. Passing an unknown long option to a systemd CLI causes it to error out, so the command fails as written.

If true (the default), lookups use the local DNS resource record cache. If false, lookups are routed to the network instead, regardless if already available in the local cache." So --cache=yes ENABLES cache use; it does not restrict the lookup to the cache. Auditor correct.

3) The flag that forces a cache-only (no-network) answer is --network=no. If false, the request is not answered from the network and will thus fail if none of the indicated sources can answer them." So --network=no yields answers only from local sources (cache/synthesis/zone/trust anchors), never the network. Auditor's proposed fix `resolvectl query --network=no example.com` is correct, and the auditor's note ("answers only from cache/synthesis, never the network") already captures the minor nuance that --network=no allows local synthesis too, not strictly the cache alone.

correction: Use a portable form. Either supply an explicit empty extension only understood per-platform, or (portable on both GNU and BSD) attach a real backup suffix: `sed -i.bak -e 's/.../.../g' file` (works on both, leaves .bak files), or use a tmpfile pattern `sed 'script' file > tmp && mv tmp file`.
